text:
As follows:

"Just as the term ‘Rangastha’ (the place of color) denotes only that very place, so too the observer, being a single pure man, sees only that. Having become one, he withdraws; there is only one nature. This one nature is the primary cause of the three worlds, and there is no second nature. Because of the distinction of forms and the distinction of species, the nature and the person (Purusha) are not separate in their activity; rather, due to their all‑pervading unity, there is conjunction. But it is not from conjunction that creation arises; rather, creation does not arise from conjunction at all."
